evals.prompt: We have twelve drivers for the European hydrogen market and they clearly interact. Build a cross-impact matrix and tell me which of these drivers actually drive the system and which are just indicators.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Restates each driver as an operational, falsifiable event before rating; Rates each ordered pair separately rather than assuming symmetry, with rationales for strong ratings; Computes influence and dependence totals with the companion script rather than by hand; Classifies items into determinants, relays, dependents and excluded; Flags asymmetric pairs and names the cells whose flip would change the classification.
expectations: Restates each driver as an operational, falsifiable event before rating
Rates each ordered pair separately rather than assuming symmetry, with rationales for strong ratings
Computes influence and dependence totals with the companion script rather than by hand
Classifies items into determinants, relays, dependents and excluded
Flags asymmetric pairs and names the cells whose flip would change the classification

evals.prompt: Run MICMAC on these ten risk variables and give me the influence/dependence map — I want to know where to act and what to just monitor.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Builds the N x N matrix and computes row and column totals in code; Produces influence and dependence rankings plus the four-quadrant classification; Reports classifications and ranges rather than decimal authority; Includes a sensitivity note on load-bearing cells.
expectations: Builds the N x N matrix and computes row and column totals in code
Produces influence and dependence rankings plus the four-quadrant classification
Reports classifications and ranges rather than decimal authority
Includes a sensitivity note on load-bearing cells

evals.prompt: If a carbon price of $100 a tonne arrives, does grid storage cost falling 50% become more or less likely? How do these events affect each other across the whole set?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Treats the question as a pairwise judgement inside a larger matrix rather than a one-off answer; Judges i to j separately from j to i and logs a rationale; Audits asymmetric pairs before computing the rankings; States that the ratings are structured judgement, not measurement.
expectations: Treats the question as a pairwise judgement inside a larger matrix rather than a one-off answer
Judges i to j separately from j to i and logs a rationale
Audits asymmetric pairs before computing the rankings
States that the ratings are structured judgement, not measurement

evals.prompt: Convene an anonymous expert panel and run iterative rounds with controlled feedback to converge on when fusion power will reach grid parity.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Does not build an interaction matrix; runs an anonymous multi-round expert elicitation and reports the group distribution (delphi-method behaviour).
expectations: Does not build an interaction matrix; runs an anonymous multi-round expert elicitation and reports the group distribution (delphi-method behaviour)

evals.prompt: Our warehouse automation goes live next year. Map the knock-on consequences ring by ring — the second and third-order effects and the unintended ones.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Does not rate mutual influence in a matrix; builds a ring-by-ring consequence map from one change (futures-wheel behaviour).
expectations: Does not rate mutual influence in a matrix; builds a ring-by-ring consequence map from one change (futures-wheel behaviour)
